checklist.notes: The past-perfect explanation, short narrative, connected-speech notation, and learner directions are appropriately demanding but accessible for B1.1.

Had + past participle is accurately related to a later past point, the forms packed/bought are correct, and the qualified weak forms /əd/, /tə/, and /ən/ are linguistically sound. One minor reference-point ambiguity is recorded.
The narrative and rehearsal language are natural, and the bracket notation is clearly explained as a practice device.
No suspicious unexplained overlap was found inside the supplied scope; the absence of external searching is explicitly recorded.
Past perfect and weak forms are introduced over the declared narrative, past-tense, sentence-stress, syllable, and word-stress closure.
The lesson is in English and every embedded identifier is authorized directly or as prerequisite context.

methods: Manual comparison of lesson wording with the supplied authoritative request and project-authored teaching payload.

Inspection of the accepted audit provenance/copyright scope without consulting external sources.

findings.description: In Section 2, ‘Her friend had already bought the tickets’ leaves its later reference point implicit, while the instruction says to draw arrows to went/arrived. A learner may be unsure whether bought should point to Mina’s arrival or another event.
findings.recommendation: State the relation explicitly, for example ‘Her friend had already bought the tickets before Mina arrived,’ and map each past-perfect event to its own later anchor.

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
